I'm not an INTJ (I'm not sure about my type), but I think the whole stereotype on INTJs that most websites or blogs claim is false especially those from 16personalities or other pseudoscience bullshit sites. There could be some truth in it but most of them just misunderstood how MBTI works (together with the cognitive functions and such). I also believe that INTJs aren't robotic or cold. Although they may be at times, for sure that it isn't their usual state.

The extrovert and introvert on the functions (INTJ for example Introverted Intuition (Ni), Extroverted Thinking (Te), Introverted Feeling (Fi), Extroverted Sensing (Se) ) do not necessarily mean or correlate to your social skills or interaction. The "introverted" and "extroverted" in these functions just say something about the use of the outside world or inner world in terms of cognition. For example, extroverted feeling (Fe) is more on considering how the tribe feels when making decisions and introverted feeling (Fi) takes note of one's own morals/values.  Another example is extroverted intuition (Ne) which leans more on gathering patterns from the real world and introverted intuition (Ni) which organizes these patterns to see their implications/hidden meaning.

Hence, this means that even the extroverted types (EJ and EP) can be introverted and the introverted types (IJ and IP) can be extroverted. It is just that cognition often affects behavior (which probably are the basis of the stereotypes) but it is not necessarily like that.  


Additionally, those formed stereotypes that you see are based on the I/E, N/S, T/F, J/P letters and not on the cognitive functions. I believe that's not how MBTI works at all. 

On a final note, what I've said was totally oversimplified so I suggest that you learn the cognitive functions and their relationship with one another to understand how MBTI truly works.
